sanskrit_shloka:
अष्टावक्र उवाच ॥
कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा ।
एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥ ९-१॥
translation: Aṣṭāvakra said: When will the opposites — the done and the undone — ever become still, and for whom? Knowing thus, through dispassion, be devoted to renunciation, free from ritual vows.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Aṣṭāvakra said: When will the opposites — the done and the undone — ever become still, and for whom? Knowing thus, through dispassion, be devoted to renunciation, free from ritual vows.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the significance of Nirveda in this chapter?
commentary_faqs.answer: Nirveda refers to a state of profound disillusionment with the world. It is presented as a necessary stage where the seeker realizes the futility of worldly desires and conflicting philosophies, leading to a natural state of peace.

commentary_faqs.question: How does Ashtavakra define the cause of Samsara?
commentary_faqs.answer: Ashtavakra explicitly states that 'Vasanas' or latent mental impressions are the very essence of Samsara. To be free from these impressions is to be free from the cycle of birth and death.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the meaning of being 'Avrati'?
commentary_faqs.answer: Being 'Avrati' means being free from the compulsion of performing rituals or religious vows. It signifies a transition from external religious performance to internal realization and stillness.

sanskrit_shloka:
कस्यापि तात धन्यस्य लोकचेष्टावलोकनात् ।
जीवितेच्छा बुभुक्षा च बुभुत्सोपशमं गताः ॥ ९-२॥
translation: O dear one, for the blessed one who has beheld the movements of the world, the desire for life, hunger for enjoyment, and thirst to know all subside.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनित्यं सर्वमेवेदं तापत्रितयदूषितम् ।
असारं निन्दितं हेयमिति निश्चित्य शाम्यति ॥ ९-३॥
translation: All this is impermanent, tainted by the threefold suffering, without essence, blameworthy and to be abandoned. Having firmly discerned this, one becomes peaceful.

sanskrit_shloka:
कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् ।
तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ ९-४॥
translation: What time, what age is there in which humans are not touched by the pairs of opposites? Disregarding them and living as things come, one attains perfection.

sanskrit_shloka:
नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा ।
दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥ ९-५॥
translation: Seeing the many opinions of great seers, saints, and yogis, and arriving at dispassion, what human being would not become still?

sanskrit_shloka:
कृत्वा मूर्तिपरिज्ञानं चैतन्यस्य न किं गुरुः ।

translation: Having discerned the manifest forms of Consciousness, is not the Guru the one who, through dispassion and equanimity, carries one across saṃsāra?

sanskrit_shloka:
पश्य भूतविकारांस्त्वं भूतमात्रान् यथार्थतः ।
तत्क्षणाद् बन्धनिर्मुक्तः स्वरूपस्थो भविष्यसि ॥ ९-७॥
translation: See the transformations of the elements as mere elements, just as they truly are. In that very instant, freed from bondage, you will abide in your own true Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
वासना एव संसार इति सर्वा विमुञ्च ताः ।
तत्त्यागो वासनात्यागात्स्थितिरद्य यथा तथा ॥ ९-८॥
translation: The vāsanās, the latent impressions, are saṃsāra itself; abandon them all. By renouncing the vāsanās, abide established in the Self, here and now, just as you are.
